cohort: 75 patients aged 20-40 years, ASA-1, with normal singleton pregnancies beyond 36 weeks of gestational age undergoing cesarean section
finding: Subcutaneous fentanyl was more effective than intravenous or intranasal fentanyl for pain management after cesarean section, with lower average pain VAS scores at recovery admission and 3 hours postoperatively.
mod_finding: This study found that subcutaneous fentanyl was an effective alternative to IV and intranasal fentanyl for pain management after cesarean section.
